text:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: sudden kv-cache size growth + tail latency spike observed in prod-eu around 1729999999. Error rate up for short-chat route. Auto-created incident #INC-2024-548

maria (sre): seeing it on the dashboards too — p50 for short-chat is fine but p95/p99 shot up to ~2.1s. paging ops increased 6x.

samir (oncall): on it. taking triage. quick check: are there any deploys in last 12h?

kevin (runtime): there was a batching heuristic tweak merged 10h ago (PR #3456) that increased pack_max_tokens and relaxed pack_timeout for continuous batching on mixed-shape routes.

ash (eng-runtime): that PR aimed to improve throughput for long-shape workloads; might be starving shorter requests by letting long ones dominate batches.

maria (sre): logs show packer queue length steady but pack composition skewed — 70% long requests end up in first slot causing cache working set to expand. Paging rate per GPU jumped.

kevin (runtime): confirming. snippet from packer metrics: 
```
packer.pack_size.histogram -> buckets: 1..8 -> heavy tail at 8 (longs)
kv_cache.pages_in /s -> +540% since 1729950000
```

samir (oncall): immediate mitigation options? revert PR, patch heuristic, or isolate route? prefer low-risk quick fixes.

ash (eng-runtime): low-risk: disable continuous batching on the short-chat route (feature flag) so small requests go to fast path. medium: lower PACK_MAX_TOKENS for the packer config. high-risk: full revert of PR.

paul (infra): can apply env overrides to packer deployment in <10min.

maria (sre): do it. step 1: flip feature flag for route short-chat -> continuous_batching=false. step 2: set PACK_MAX_TOKENS=2048 -> 1024 if needed. step 3: monitor paging and latencies.

kevin (runtime): prepping a config rollout. command to apply now: 
```
kubectl -n inference set env deployment/packer PACK_MAX_TOKENS=1024 --record
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/packer
```

samir (oncall): go for the feature flag flip first, then the env change if no improvement. ash, can you flip the flag?

ash (eng-runtime): flipping flag for route=short-chat to OFF now.

incidents-bot: Action logged by ash at 1729990160: feature_flag.short_chat.continuous_batching=false

julia (support): customers hitting higher tail latency: small set of high-value customers on europe cluster. I'm preparing proactive comms.

kevin (runtime): monitoring dashboards... paging ops dropping within 3m. p95 down from 2.1s -> 760ms. kv cache resident size decreasing.

maria (sre): good sign. confirm error rates?

julia (support): error rate dropped, but 5 customers still reporting occasional timeouts during the spike window (1729986000-1729990000). I'll open tickets and patch message.

tony (csm): please include list of affected accounts and recommended credit / mitigation options. I'll help triage customer comms.

samir (oncall): second mitigation: lower PACK_MAX_TOKENS to 1024 to reduce dominance of long requests. kevin, proceed when stable.

kevin (runtime): applying env override now. 

incidents-bot: Action logged by kevin at 1729990480: set PACK_MAX_TOKENS=1024 and restarted packer deployment.

maria (sre): metrics: p95 now 540ms, paging down to near-baseline. continuous_batching off cut long-request packing in mixed batches.

ash (eng-runtime): quick root cause: new heuristic allowed larger packs and higher token thresholds which in presence of skewed arrival (bursts of long requests) caused pack composition imbalance and inflated KV working set -> aggressive paging -> perf cliff for short requests that expect in-cache reads.

samir (oncall): no rollback needed for now, mitigations worked. create a short-lived runbook for reverting if things regress.

maria (sre): agree. also we should enable per-route batching caps so one shape can't monopolize packers. adding to follow-up.

kevin (runtime): created hotfix branch that adjusts packer selection weights and adds short-request priority. branch: hotfix/pack-weight-172999. PR filed: https://git.internal/r/PR/4389.

julia (support): customer list for outreach: acct: acme-eu, finbot-inc, legalai-eu, chatify. I'll start outreach. recommended credit: 1 week of priority QPS for impacted customers + formal apology.

tony (csm): ack — I'll coordinate emails once you draft messages. include basic root-cause and what we did.

maria (sre): immediate post-incident tasks:
- create incident ticket and severity summary (I have a template)
- collect heap/profile for packer during window
- add traffic shaping rule to avoid packer hot loops

samir (oncall): handing off to kevin for next 8h on-call follow-up (watch for recurrence, finalize PR). I'm off shift at 1730001200.

kevin (runtime): taking handoff. will watch for oscillation and finish the fairness tweak.

incidents-bot: HANDOFF: samir -> kevin at 1730001200 (notes: mitigations applied, monitoring stable, PR open).

paul (infra): we'll also bump node IO limits on prod-eu if paging resurges. prepping runbook.

ash (eng-runtime): next actions for engineering:
1) revert heuristic change in main only if PR shows other regressions.
2) implement per-route pack caps + priority token bucket.
3) add chaos test for mixed shape bursts.

maria (sre): assign postmortem to samir/kevin/ash. include timeline, root cause, customer impact, and remediation owners.

julia (support): draft sent for review to tony and maria. will cc legal if needed.

kevin (runtime): quick note: if you see paging>baseline + pack_size skew -> flip short-chat batching off (feature flag) as an emergency step. Documented in runbook.

maria (sre): moving incident to monitoring mode. severity -> sev3 (customer-impacting transient), but we should still publish a blameless postmortem.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED: #INC-2024-548 severity set to sev3 by maria at 1730001400.

samir (oncall): leaving final note: thanks all. big thumbs to ash/kevin for quick flips. follow-ups: schedule engineering retro, finalize PR, and customer outreach.

kevin (runtime): will follow up with timeline and link to perf diffs tomorrow.

paul (infra): closing infra tasks after 24h of stability.

julia (support): will keep customers updated; I'll post a summary here when messages go out.

maria (sre): resolved for now — moving to post-incident tracking. :white_check_mark:
